# Design critique

Read the brief, audience and desired feeling first. Inspect the result and actual preview.
Observation → communication effect → importance → proposed change → recheck.
Assess brief/meaning, visual organization, historical/cultural context, editable production and process separately.
Personal taste is not objective error. Do not produce findings about an image you have not seen.
A score or search ranking does not prove design quality. Technical checks do not replace aesthetic judgment.

## Evidence-required findings

Each finding records artifact/revision, inspected flat view and pixel/use size, exact region/text, literal observation, applicable brief criterion, likely communication effect, severity, proposed correction, actual comparison/recheck and uncertainty. Classify as demonstrated failure, risk/uncertainty, interpretation or preference. Audience effect without real testing is a hypothesis. Never claim expert, reader or community endorsement from AI inspection.

Separate brief/content, hierarchy/typography, composition/color, contextual history, rights/safety, editability/production and human acceptance. A blocking right, save failure, required-use defect or safety failure cannot be averaged away. If no demonstrated defect exists, state that instead of manufacturing one. Search scores describe lexical relevance only.

## Required views and typography

Inspect flat artwork at final and smallest brief-required sizes; mockups are supplementary. Compare exact copy and punctuation, glyph coverage, kerning, leading, margins, optical alignment and actual contrast. Record requested/actual fonts and substitutions; size values in a source are not measured readability. Screen contrast evidence does not automatically certify print or raster-cover WCAG conformity. Native inspection is required only when native editability is claimed; SVG is not PSD proof.

## Comparison, revision and advancement

Use the same brief/views for [original A/control examples](../../examples/learning-guide-cover/CRITIQUE.md). The control is not client work; multiple variables changed, so no single-variable causal proof. Require a retained before, actual revised source/export, specific change and same-condition recheck. A proposal alone does not advance a learner. Review each observable module criterion against submitted evidence; missing mandatory artifacts lead to revise/blocked/not-assessed, not a taste score or degree-equivalence outcome. No learner submissions have been assessed by authoring this curriculum.

## Context and abstention

Name tradition/place/period/language/audience only when supported. Explain source context before adaptation; avoid culture-as-decoration and universal European-modernist standards. Unfamiliar scripts, sacred/restricted symbols and identity-sensitive uses require qualified contextual review; do not invent community authority.

Unseen image: provide a checklist, no pixel findings. Missing source: critique visible output only, editability unverified. Unsupported historical claim: qualify/remove it. Unavailable native route: blocked, not simulated. Missing approval: human pending. Unknown rights: affected asset redistribution unresolved; original replacements permitted without clearance claims.

## Recovery

Keep original/rejected routes and failure receipts. Use new task-owned versions, protect unsaved documents, never overwrite another person's files, silently replace fonts or close unrelated documents. Save/reopen/export failures stay separate from aesthetic evaluation. This wave's Photoshop native gate is blocked by user decision; do not execute scripts to bypass it.

# From foundations to portfolio
This is an original research-derived study plan, not a copied syllabus or degree equivalent. Module numbers do not prescribe weeks or durations; adapt depth to the learner’s current level.

## Competency advancement
Authored curriculum only; no learner outcomes assessed. Complete the linked module's concrete artifacts, observable criteria and actual before/after critique/recheck before advancing. Prerequisites are evidence dependencies, not time served. A blocked tool/native output remains blocked, not passed by reading. Rights, safety, production and human acceptance are separate from aesthetic judgment. See [assessment](../assessment/critique.md).

Canonical exercise contracts: [01 form](../exercises/01.md), [02 color](../exercises/02.md), [03 typography](../exercises/03.md), [04 context](../exercises/04.md), [05 image-making](../exercises/05.md), [06 identity](../exercises/06.md), [07 series](../exercises/07.md), [08 editorial](../exercises/08.md), [09 preproduction](../exercises/09.md), [10 motion identity](../exercises/10.md), [11 editing](../exercises/11.md), [12 case study](../exercises/12.md). Each specifies prerequisites, objectives, deliverables, observable criteria, critique/revision and retained evidence. The summaries below are orientation, not completion receipts. Source references retain their individual imported/reviewed status; no university affiliation or copied syllabus implied.

## 01. Visual perception and form
Negative space, value, emphasis, rhythm and balance; separate observation from interpretation.

**Suggested deliverable:** A formal analysis of one poster and three small compositions.

**Sources:** [S21: Getty formal analysis learning resources](https://www.getty.edu/education/teachers/classroom_resources/formal_analysis.html); [S01: RISD Graphic Design BFA](https://www.risd.edu/academics/graphic-design/bachelors-program)

## 02. Color in context
Explore color relationships experimentally; distinguish perception from file-profile problems.

**Suggested deliverable:** Six background experiments using the same colors and a production-profile note.

**Sources:** [S22: Albers Foundation Interaction of Color](https://www.albersfoundation.org/alberses/teaching/interaction-of-color); [S23: Albers Foundation One Color Becomes Two](https://www.albersfoundation.org/learning/workshops/one-color-becomes-two)

## 03. Typography
Letterforms, spacing, hierarchy and long/short text; test the characters required by the intended language.

**Suggested deliverable:** Three typography-only posters and a process journal.

**Sources:** [S02: RISD Graphic Design course catalogue](https://www.risd.edu/academics/graphic-design/courses); [S16: CMU Typography One: Type as Image syllabus](https://www.cmu.edu/teaching/designteach/design/syllabus/samples-creative/TypographySyllabus.pdf)

## 04. Reading through art and design history
Distinguish movements, schools and traditions; separate sourced context from contemporary proposals.

**Suggested deliverable:** A research card comparing two approaches.

**Sources:** [S27: MoMA Bauhaus](https://www.moma.org/collection/terms/bauhaus); [S33: MoMA The New Typography](https://www.moma.org/calendar/exhibitions/1013); [S47: SALT Painter Sabiha Rüştü Bozcalı](https://saltonline.org/tr/ressam-sabiha-rustu-bozcali-1256)

## 05. Image-making and photomontage
Meaning, material, photography, illustration, masks and source rights.

**Suggested deliverable:** An editable cover composition and source list.

**Sources:** [S05: CalArts Graphic Design BFA](https://calarts.edu/academics/programs-and-degrees/bfa-graphic-design); [S31: MoMA Dada: chance, collage, photomontage and assemblage](https://www.moma.org/collection/terms/dada/chance-creations-collage-photomontage-and-assemblage)

## 06. Logos and visual identity
Treat a brand as more than a single mark; define constants and variants.

**Suggested deliverable:** A logo family, one-color tests and a short identity guide.

**Sources:** [S02: RISD Graphic Design course catalogue](https://www.risd.edu/academics/graphic-design/courses); [S18: Ringling Motion Design course catalogue](https://catalog.ringling.edu/motion-design)

## 07. Posters, flyers and social series
Preserve one message across different sizes and content lengths.

**Suggested deliverable:** A poster, flyer and four-part social series.

**Sources:** [S07: UAL LCC Graphic and Media Design](https://www.arts.ac.uk/subjects/communication-and-graphic-design/undergraduate/ba-hons-graphic-and-media-design-lcc); [S40: Cooper Hewitt: How Posters Work](https://www.cooperhewitt.org/2015/02/05/cooper-hewitt-to-present-special-exhibition-how-posters-work/)

## 08. Editorial design and covers
Grids, reading order, page styles and relationships between content and material.

**Suggested deliverable:** An eight-page publication, cover and production check.

**Sources:** [S11: ECAL Graphic Design Bachelor](https://ecal.ch/en/courses-and-research/bachelor/bachelor-graphic-design/); [S14: Bilkent Graphic Design central catalogue](https://catalog.bilkent.edu.tr/dep/dc72.html)

## 09. Motion preproduction
Define the purpose of movement; develop storyboards, styleframes and animatics.

**Suggested deliverable:** A six-frame storyboard and short animatic.

**Sources:** [S18: Ringling Motion Design course catalogue](https://catalog.ringling.edu/motion-design); [S20: SCAD Motion Media Design BFA catalogue](https://catalog.scad.edu/school-animation-motion/motion-media-design/motion-media-design-bfa/)

## 10. Motion identity
Typography, transitions, rhythm, holds and translating a visual system into time.

**Suggested deliverable:** An approximately 10-second motion experiment for the same brand.

**Sources:** [S18: Ringling Motion Design course catalogue](https://catalog.ringling.edu/motion-design); [S20: SCAD Motion Media Design BFA catalogue](https://catalog.scad.edu/school-animation-motion/motion-media-design/motion-media-design-bfa/)

## 11. Editing, sound and captions
Clip selection, narrative, audio relationships and readable captions.

**Suggested deliverable:** An approximately 30-second edit with project and output checks.

**Sources:** [S20: SCAD Motion Media Design BFA catalogue](https://catalog.scad.edu/school-animation-motion/motion-media-design/motion-media-design-bfa/); [S14: Bilkent Graphic Design central catalogue](https://catalog.bilkent.edu.tr/dep/dc72.html)

## 12. Portfolio and critique
Research question, alternatives, choice rationale, revision and self-assessment.

**Suggested deliverable:** One complete case study with before/after comparisons and production evidence.

**Sources:** [S04: Yale Graphic Design MFA](https://art.yale.edu/program/graphic-design); [S05: CalArts Graphic Design BFA](https://calarts.edu/academics/programs-and-degrees/bfa-graphic-design); [S10: KABK Graphic Design programme description](https://www.kabk.nl/en/programmes/bachelor/graphic-design/programme-description)

## 01. Visual perception and form
Negative space, value, emphasis, rhythm and balance; separate observation from interpretation.

### Prerequisites
None. Use original shapes or a lawfully viewable image; do not redistribute third-party images.
### Objective
Describe five visible relationships without substituting preference for evidence.
### Deliverable
One annotated analysis card and three original 600x600 SVG compositions with PNG views.
### Observable criteria
Identify line/shape/value/space and emphasis by region; label observation versus interpretation; retain the same elements across compositions so hierarchy changes are visible.
### Critique and revision
Compare two flat views, name one hierarchy risk and one preference, revise one spacing/scale variable and recheck at 150x150.
### Retained evidence
Brief, original/revised SVG and full/reduced views, region-specific critique, actual changes and unresolved uncertainty. Use [assessment](../assessment/critique.md); no learner outcome is implied by authorship.

**Suggested deliverable:** A formal analysis of one poster and three small compositions.

**Sources:** [S21: Getty formal analysis learning resources](https://www.getty.edu/education/teachers/classroom_resources/formal_analysis.html); [S01: RISD Graphic Design BFA](https://www.risd.edu/academics/graphic-design/bachelors-program)
lessons.title: 01. Visual perception and form

## 02. Color in context
Explore color relationships experimentally; distinguish perception from file-profile problems.

### Prerequisites
[01](01.md): demonstrate observation versus interpretation.
### Objective
Compare contextual color appearance while preserving the inner color's numerical value.
### Deliverable
Six 600x600 original SVG/PNG background experiments and a color-profile note.
### Observable criteria
Record exact inner/background values; same inner value across variants; identify observed appearance separately from file/profile facts and unsupported universal emotion claims.
### Critique and revision
Compare a selected pair at the same size, change only one background, re-export and describe the observed difference or no difference without inventing a viewer sample.
### Retained evidence
Before/after sources/views, values, renderer/profile limitations and [criterion-separated critique](../assessment/critique.md).

**Suggested deliverable:** Six background experiments using the same colors and a production-profile note.

**Sources:** [S22: Albers Foundation Interaction of Color](https://www.albersfoundation.org/alberses/teaching/interaction-of-color); [S23: Albers Foundation One Color Becomes Two](https://www.albersfoundation.org/learning/workshops/one-color-becomes-two)
lessons.title: 02. Color in context

lessons.markdown:
## 03. Typography
Letterforms, spacing, hierarchy and long/short text; test the characters required by the intended language.

### Prerequisites
[01](01.md): evidence-based hierarchy description.
### Objective
Preserve exact copy and glyph coverage while testing typographic reading order and optical spacing.
### Deliverable
Three original typography-only 1200x1600 posters in editable SVG plus 300x400 views; font/fallback journal.
### Observable criteria
Title/supporting copy transcribed exactly; no clipping/collision at either size; observed kerning/leading/margins recorded; font substitution and script uncertainty explicit. Required unfamiliar scripts need qualified review.
### Critique and revision
Hold content/layout fixed, revise one spacing or scale variable; compare before/after at both sizes using [assessment](../assessment/critique.md). Reader comprehension is untested unless actual responses retained.
### Retained evidence
Copy brief, font inventory without binaries, original/revised sources and exports, glyph/optical findings and recheck. See [typography record](../../atlas/foundations/typography-hierarchy.md).

**Suggested deliverable:** Three typography-only posters and a process journal.

**Sources:** [S02: RISD Graphic Design course catalogue](https://www.risd.edu/academics/graphic-design/courses); [S16: CMU Typography One: Type as Image syllabus](https://www.cmu.edu/teaching/designteach/design/syllabus/samples-creative/TypographySyllabus.pdf)
lessons.title: 03. Typography

lessons.markdown:
## 04. Reading through art and design history
Distinguish movements, schools and traditions; separate sourced context from contemporary proposals.

### Prerequisites
[01](01.md): separating description from interpretation.
### Objective
Resolve two historical claims to actual source passages without conflating a school, movement, technique or tradition.
### Deliverable
Two Markdown research cards, each with exact source ID/page/locator/access date/limits and an original contemporary proposal.
### Observable criteria
Correct record categories; quoted/paraphrased claim supported by actual inspected passage; imported versus independent review and text/image/font rights separate. Unsupported period/place or inaccessible source stays unverified.
### Critique and revision
Compare categories/context, identify one overgeneralization, revise claim scope and check source again. Do not promote an entire corpus or universal style ranking.
### Retained evidence
Before/after cards, short support passages, failure/uncertainty log and [critique](../assessment/critique.md); no third-party images copied.

**Suggested deliverable:** A research card comparing two approaches.

**Sources:** [S27: MoMA Bauhaus](https://www.moma.org/collection/terms/bauhaus); [S33: MoMA The New Typography](https://www.moma.org/calendar/exhibitions/1013); [S47: SALT Painter Sabiha Rüştü Bozcalı](https://saltonline.org/tr/ressam-sabiha-rustu-bozcali-1256)
lessons.title: 04. Reading through art and design history

lessons.markdown:
## 05. Image-making and photomontage
Meaning, material, photography, illustration, masks and source rights.

### Prerequisites
[01](01.md), [03](03.md): hierarchy and exact typography.
### Objective
Construct an editable original image relationship with a traceable asset inventory.
### Deliverable
1200x1600 cover master and full/300x400 views plus asset-rights list. Original vector shapes are allowed when photo rights are unknown; native layered file only if actually authorized/available.
### Observable criteria
Elements remain independently editable; exact copy and required-size hierarchy intact; edges/lighting assessed relative to declared collage or realism goal; asset ownership/rights separate from source citation. SVG does not prove native PSD layers.
### Critique and revision
Compare before/after of one mask/edge/scale change and inspect full/reduced outputs; classify defect versus expressive preference using [assessment](../assessment/critique.md).
### Retained evidence
Original/revised masters/views, asset inventory, editability method, actual checks and blocked native state. Current-wave Photoshop is blocked by user decision; no script workaround.

**Suggested deliverable:** An editable cover composition and source list.

**Sources:** [S05: CalArts Graphic Design BFA](https://calarts.edu/academics/programs-and-degrees/bfa-graphic-design); [S31: MoMA Dada: chance, collage, photomontage and assemblage](https://www.moma.org/collection/terms/dada/chance-creations-collage-photomontage-and-assemblage)
lessons.title: 05. Image-making and photomontage

lessons.markdown:
## 06. Logos and visual identity
Treat a brand as more than a single mark; define constants and variants.

### Prerequisites
[02](02.md), [03](03.md), [04](04.md): color, typography and claim scope.
### Objective
Build an identity system that meets declared use conditions, not just a geometric mark.
### Deliverable
Three original concepts, selected provisional editable mark/wordmark, BRAND.md and exact-size flat specimens. Declare smallest use, one-color/reverse/background and long-content cases before testing; e.g. 32px and 256px screens when relevant.
### Observable criteria
Distinct concepts/rejections retained; optical kerning/counters documented; required specimens legible/not clipped; cultural/script and asset/font rights uncertainty explicit. Trademark screening is not legal clearance; human/native gates separate.
### Critique and revision
Follow [identity operations](../../workflows/identity.md); retain before/after optical correction and same-size rechecks. Do not invent an accepted identity outcome.
### Retained evidence
Brief, concepts, refinement views, rights inventory, use manifest, [critique](../assessment/critique.md), native blocked/unrun receipt and explicit human decision or pending.

**Suggested deliverable:** A logo family, one-color tests and a short identity guide.

**Sources:** [S02: RISD Graphic Design course catalogue](https://www.risd.edu/academics/graphic-design/courses); [S18: Ringling Motion Design course catalogue](https://catalog.ringling.edu/motion-design)
lessons.title: 06. Logos and visual identity

lessons.markdown:
## 07. Posters, flyers and social series
Preserve one message across different sizes and content lengths.

### Prerequisites
[03](03.md), [06](06.md): typographic/system constraints.
### Objective
Adapt hierarchy across formats without stretching or losing essential information.
### Deliverable
Original 1200x1600 poster, 600x800 flyer and four 1080x1080 social cards with editable sources and flat previews; include shortest/longest headline specimens.
### Observable criteria
Exact event/title/date/place copy; no collision/clipping; constants/variants named; essential text inspectable at declared display sizes, not just a mockup. Label situated communication choices rather than universal style superiority.
### Critique and revision
Compare long/short variants, revise one overflow/hierarchy risk and recheck all affected formats with [assessment](../assessment/critique.md).
### Retained evidence
Content fixture, before/after sources/previews, size manifest, actual rechecks and rights/font limitations.

**Suggested deliverable:** A poster, flyer and four-part social series.

**Sources:** [S07: UAL LCC Graphic and Media Design](https://www.arts.ac.uk/subjects/communication-and-graphic-design/undergraduate/ba-hons-graphic-and-media-design-lcc); [S40: Cooper Hewitt: How Posters Work](https://www.cooperhewitt.org/2015/02/05/cooper-hewitt-to-present-special-exhibition-how-posters-work/)
lessons.title: 07. Posters, flyers and social series

lessons.markdown:
## 08. Editorial design and covers
Grids, reading order, page styles and relationships between content and material.

### Prerequisites
[03](03.md), [04](04.md), [07](07.md): type, source scope and adaptable layouts.
### Objective
Carry editorial content through brief, distinct concepts, provisional choice and checked publication layouts.
### Deliverable
Eight-page digital publication with declared page dimensions, three cover directions, selected editable cover and full/reduced exports; use [original cover example](../../examples/learning-guide-cover/README.md), not a copied design.
### Observable criteria
Reading order/page styles consistent; exact copy present; required-size cover check; rejection rationale and rights inventory retained; no press-ready claim without actual bleed/profile/print tests.
### Critique and revision
Follow [cover workflow](../../workflows/cover-editorial.md), identify one page/cover risk, revise and compare before/after under the same conditions using [assessment](../assessment/critique.md).
### Retained evidence
Brief, concepts, publication/source files, exports and revision log; native proof/human acceptance unrun or pending unless actually demonstrated.

**Suggested deliverable:** An eight-page publication, cover and production check.

**Sources:** [S11: ECAL Graphic Design Bachelor](https://ecal.ch/en/courses-and-research/bachelor/bachelor-graphic-design/); [S14: Bilkent Graphic Design central catalogue](https://catalog.bilkent.edu.tr/dep/dc72.html)
lessons.title: 08. Editorial design and covers

## 09. Motion preproduction
Define the purpose of movement; develop storyboards, styleframes and animatics.

### Prerequisites
[01](01.md), [07](07.md): visible hierarchy and format adaptation.
### Objective
Explain why movement/holds convey a message and retain a static alternative.
### Deliverable
Six 1920x1080 original storyboard/styleframes plus 6-10 second animatic with declared frame rate, or an explicitly blocked animatic and editable timing sheet when tools unavailable.
### Observable criteria
Each shot has purpose/time; exact text and adequate declared holds; motion avoids flashing/discomfort risks; static sequence communicates core content. Tool absence does not become completed video.
### Critique and revision
Review actual frames/timing, change one hold/transition, compare before/after; if playback unavailable, abstain on temporal perception using [assessment](../assessment/critique.md).
### Retained evidence
Sources, frames, timing sheet, actual playback/export receipt or blocked state, revisions and rights list.

**Suggested deliverable:** A six-frame storyboard and short animatic.

**Sources:** [S18: Ringling Motion Design course catalogue](https://catalog.ringling.edu/motion-design); [S20: SCAD Motion Media Design BFA catalogue](https://catalog.scad.edu/school-animation-motion/motion-media-design/motion-media-design-bfa/)
lessons.title: 09. Motion preproduction

lessons.markdown:
## 10. Motion identity
Typography, transitions, rhythm, holds and translating a visual system into time.

### Prerequisites
[06](06.md), [09](09.md): identity uses and motion preproduction.
### Objective
Translate declared identity constants into time without losing identification or required text.
### Deliverable
Approximately 10-second 1920x1080 motion source/export at declared frame rate, static alternative and first/mid/final frames. Native operation only with an authorized live route.
### Observable criteria
Constants/variants identifiable; glyphs/copy preserved; holds/transitions checked in actual playback; no flash-based essential message; export duration/dimensions verified. Static source alone is not motion proof.
### Critique and revision
Compare one timing/transition change in actual before/after playback, document tradeoff and recheck; unavailable playback/native tools remain blocked, per [assessment](../assessment/critique.md).
### Retained evidence
Brand rules, sources, frames, timing/export receipts, revision comparison and untested native/audience states.

**Suggested deliverable:** An approximately 10-second motion experiment for the same brand.

**Sources:** [S18: Ringling Motion Design course catalogue](https://catalog.ringling.edu/motion-design); [S20: SCAD Motion Media Design BFA catalogue](https://catalog.scad.edu/school-animation-motion/motion-media-design/motion-media-design-bfa/)
lessons.title: 10. Motion identity

lessons.markdown:
## 11. Editing, sound and captions
Clip selection, narrative, audio relationships and readable captions.

### Prerequisites
[03](03.md), [09](09.md): typography and timing.
### Objective
Assemble a narrative with synchronized readable captions and controlled audio relationships.
### Deliverable
Approximately 30-second 1920x1080 edit with declared frame rate, editable project, video export, UTF-8 SRT captions and original/authorized media inventory. Missing tools mean blocked output, not synthesized execution evidence.
### Observable criteria
Caption text/time matches actual speech; no clipping in declared safe regions; overlaps/gaps and audio peaks reviewed during actual playback; every clip/sound right recorded. Proper names/diacritics preserved; unfamiliar language requires qualified review.
### Critique and revision
Compare before/after of one cut/caption/audio issue, playback same segment, retain actual recheck and [criterion classification](../assessment/critique.md).
### Retained evidence
Project/media provenance, exports/captions, timing/audio findings, revised segment and blocked/unverified production states.

**Suggested deliverable:** An approximately 30-second edit with project and output checks.

**Sources:** [S20: SCAD Motion Media Design BFA catalogue](https://catalog.scad.edu/school-animation-motion/motion-media-design/motion-media-design-bfa/); [S14: Bilkent Graphic Design central catalogue](https://catalog.bilkent.edu.tr/dep/dc72.html)
lessons.title: 11. Editing, sound and captions

lessons.markdown:
## 12. Portfolio and critique
Research question, alternatives, choice rationale, revision and self-assessment.

### Prerequisites
[04](04.md) and at least one completed production module [05](05.md), [06](06.md), [08](08.md), [10](10.md) or [11](11.md), with actual submitted evidence. Blocked native gates stay labeled.
### Objective
Present a traceable case study that distinguishes authored work, observed results and acceptance.
### Deliverable
Markdown case study, source/support ledger, three retained routes when brief requires, selected editable source, actual flat required-size outputs and at least one before/after revision.
### Observable criteria
Each decision resolves to an artifact/criterion; actual revision and recheck present; source/rights, software/artifact/native/human gates separate. No fabricated audience response, degree equivalent or mastery from authorship.
### Critique and revision
Run [assessment](../assessment/critique.md), identify one weak evidence claim or design risk, amend case study or artifact and recheck. Explicit reviewer/human response only if actually supplied.
### Retained evidence
Original/revised files, failures/partial outputs, raw responses privately if authorized, sanitized manifest, known limitations and exact next acceptance gate.

**Suggested deliverable:** One complete case study with before/after comparisons and production evidence.

**Sources:** [S04: Yale Graphic Design MFA](https://art.yale.edu/program/graphic-design); [S05: CalArts Graphic Design BFA](https://calarts.edu/academics/programs-and-degrees/bfa-graphic-design); [S10: KABK Graphic Design programme description](https://www.kabk.nl/en/programmes/bachelor/graphic-design/programme-description)

movements.limits: Digital strokes do not model hand craft, labor, industrial production or object use. This is original interpretation, not a Morris reproduction. S24 retains its canonical unreviewed status.

regions.explanation: Unequal paired strokes form a self-authored leaf. Count controls repetitions, not a historical motif.

regions.explanation: Calm original type stays independent of ornament; compare the typography-only state.

regions.explanation: The white interval separates the making rhythm from information. Repetition is a material proposal, not source history.
regions.label: Unit/field interval

movements.teaching: Compare an original hand-like repeated leaf unit with a typography-only communication field. Change repeat spacing and stroke weight: does material rhythm help this fictional workshop message? Make the process visible rather than treating a botanical motif as the whole movement.

movements.limits: A curve is not the whole international movement; geometric examples and varied regional contexts are not modeled. No named artist replica. See unreviewed S25.

regions.explanation: The exact phrase is actual system-font text, not an imported lettering specimen.

regions.explanation: Original leaf ellipses share the stem rhythm but do not identify every Art Nouveau work.

movements.teaching: Vary the bow of a self-authored stem and the contour width. Compare how an image contour and a headline field share a surface; retain three contour abstractions without tracing a plant photograph.

movements.limits: Materials, historical-modern combinations and colonial context exceed this digital diagram. No exotic borrowed motifs or named-work copy. S26 remains unreviewed.

regions.explanation: Centered tiers contract upward; two independent dimensions govern rhythm.

regions.explanation: The original announcement remains outside the stepped silhouette.

regions.explanation: An explicit centerline lets you test symmetry without claiming it is universal.
regions.label: Symmetry axis

movements.teaching: Edit step count and width in an original stepped construction. Compare monochrome versus color while keeping form; test symmetry, linear rhythm and a calm information base. Gold and black are not requirements.
movements.title: Stepped rhythm

movements.limits: Publication, architecture and social aims are not modeled; color recipe is not the whole movement. Actual S28 status is unchanged.

regions.explanation: A variable vertical partition changes the two areas and their boundary.
regions.label: Unequal color fields

regions.explanation: The small original label anchors this diagram to our teaching project, not a historical painting.
regions.label: Retained original identity

regions.explanation: Horizontal and vertical strokes cross without decorative diagonals; test interval relationships.
regions.label: Orthogonal crossing

movements.teaching: Change the partition and boundary weight of an original orthogonal color-field proposal. Compare unequal areas and remove color to test hierarchy. This complements the preserved pilot plane reconstruction, not a familiar painting copy.
movements.title: Asymmetrical plane intervals

movements.limits: Political context, production and social function remain larger than this display. Contemporary proposal only; S29 is unreviewed, no invented political endorsement.

regions.explanation: The band rotates around its center, suggesting a proposed reading direction.
regions.label: Directional band

regions.explanation: Actual exact copy stays level rather than becoming unreadable decoration.

regions.label: Production note

movements.teaching: Change the direction band and information-block scale for an original public-interest message. Explain the communication purpose of each hierarchy; a red diagonal alone is not historical Constructivism.
movements.title: Direction for a public message

movements.limits: Not a Malevich reconstruction or a universal formula; original formal study only. Historical aims and S30 review are separate from Constructivism.

regions.explanation: The square has no depicted object; rotation changes its tension with the field.

regions.explanation: The circle radius is independently controlled. Formal contrast is not a historical aim by itself.
regions.label: Circular counterweight

regions.explanation: A third bar makes the empty gap measurable rather than filling every region.
regions.label: Bar interval

movements.teaching: Move and rotate three original geometric forms. Predict the weight of their intervals, retain six balance states and explain why this nonrepresentational study is different from a communication-engineering proposal.
movements.title: Tension without representation

movements.limits: Original fragments only; no newspaper scans, historical slogans or copied art. Antiwar/social critique belongs in sourced context, not a randomness success claim. S31 remains unreviewed.

regions.explanation: An integer seed reproduces original rectangles and a cut form; no external asset enters the collage.
regions.label: Chance fragments

regions.explanation: Exact editable words supply a question; the chance rule cannot supply its meaning.
regions.label: Critical phrase

regions.explanation: Switch off chance and compare the same fragments before making a claim about disruption.

movements.teaching: Record a deterministic seed and compare planned versus chance placement of original fragments. Edit the critical phrase and explain the cultural question; randomness alone does not establish Dada.
movements.title: Chance against a claim

movements.limits: No named artwork replica, dream diagnosis or universal method. Unconscious/liberation context remains sourced and unreviewed at S32.

regions.explanation: The original cup changes relative size, creating a proposed conceptual encounter.
regions.label: Altered vessel scale

regions.explanation: The words make your premise inspectable; interpretation is not a diagnosis.
regions.label: Encounter phrase

regions.explanation: A stable original arch acts as the comparison anchor for scale and lift.
regions.label: Arch relationship

movements.teaching: Write a short encounter, then change an original vessel's relative scale and lift beside an arch. Explain the uncanny relationship while retaining an independent headline. Flying objects alone are not the movement.
movements.title: An unexpected relationship

movements.limits: Contemporary original system-font proposal, not a historical poster. Actual readership and S33 passage review remain separate.

regions.explanation: A visible rule gives the text blocks a spatial anchor; alignment is a controlled decision.
regions.label: Alignment rule

regions.explanation: Title lines are editable text, not an image or language-neutral pattern.
regions.label: Actual title glyphs

regions.explanation: Supporting facts stay readable in their own block; compare retrieval rather than assuming a neutral style.
regions.label: Date/place hierarchy

movements.teaching: Transcribe the exact announcement and glyphs. Compare centered and asymmetrical information order by changing alignment, title size and leading. No imported font; asymmetry never excuses clipping or illegibility.
movements.title: The page is an open field

movements.limits: No branded packaging, characters or named artist replication. Popular/commercial culture context at S35 is unreviewed; no universal Pop recipe.

regions.explanation: The repeated unit is our original object, not a commercial package.
regions.label: Repeated ordinary cup

regions.explanation: Editable words change the interpretation; palette alone cannot establish critique.

regions.explanation: Distinct framed intervals let you compare count and order without flashing.
regions.label: Panel sequence

movements.teaching: Repeat a self-authored cup across original panels. Change panel count and narrative label; compare repetition with one object, and explain whether the sequence means more than a palette change.
movements.title: An ordinary object, several narratives

movements.limits: No measured perceptual response, animation or historical replica. Static patterns can still cause discomfort; quiet alternative is always available. S36 remains unreviewed.

regions.explanation: Separated lines repeat without temporal modulation; no flashing is generated.

regions.explanation: The instruction remains outside optical tension and warns about discomfort.

regions.explanation: The field is spatially bounded; compare pitch while holding width constant.

movements.title: Static spacing, not flashing

movements.limits: Historical Minimalism in art is not minimal marketing design. No material, spatial-installation or named-work reproduction claim. S37 remains unreviewed.

regions.explanation: Count removes whole units; a staged reduction changes shape detail instead of recoloring it.

regions.explanation: The small original label is not a claim that less is universally better.
regions.label: Declared meaning

regions.explanation: Blank field is a real spatial relationship, but not physical material presence.
regions.label: Empty interval

movements.teaching: Reduce an original object arrangement through three stages, then change interval and object count. Record when identification or meaning is lost. This screen study cannot demonstrate material or physical presence.

records.contemporary_application: Make materials and production methods the rationale for visual decisions in a publication or product identity; texture should serve more than decoration.

records.visual_principles: Relationships between materials, making and use; the close connection between craft and design.

records.contemporary_application: Create an original poster that unites the headline and main image through a shared line system, with a simpler mark for small uses.

records.contemporary_application: Try stepped forms and rhythmic letter spacing in a cover or event identity; choose a solution that also works in one color.

records.contemporary_application: Build a critical cover composition from your own elements that questions the language of current news.
records.exercise: Compare a planned composition with one produced through a chance rule; explain how chance changes meaning.

records.contemporary_application: Create a cover with original object relationships around one central idea; transform the same conceptual relationship in motion.
records.exercise: Choose an encounter from five minutes of free writing and turn it into a poster with a clear headline hierarchy.

records.limits: Surrealism is more than flying objects. Do not assume every work uses the same method.

records.limits: Helvetica and claims of cultural neutrality are not mandatory; choose according to font, language and context.

records.contemporary_application: Design a social series that centers an ordinary object without copying copyrighted characters or branded packaging.
records.exercise: Show one object through three narratives; explain whether repetition creates meaning or merely changes color.
records.filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.
records.historical_context: Tate explains Pop Art through developments centered in Britain and the United States in the 1950s and 1960s that engaged with popular and commercial culture.
records.limits: Do not reduce Pop Art to one artist repetition scheme or comic-book dots.
records.visual_principles: Everyday objects, advertising and packaging language, distinct forms and varied approaches to mass culture.

records.contemporary_application: Create an original optical field separate from the primary information; plan effect controls and a static alternative for motion.
records.exercise: Make six comparisons by changing just one variable in the same geometric field.
records.filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

records.limits: Check the risk of rapid flashing and discomfort; keep readable text outside optical tension.
records.visual_principles: Repetition, spacing, scale, contrast and perceptual change.

records.contemporary_application: Reduce a cover to essential elements while preserving meaning, information hierarchy and the production surface.
records.exercise: Take a design through three stages of reduction and record when meaning is lost.
records.filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.
records.historical_context: Tate connects Minimalism in art with the United States in the 1960s, simple geometric forms, materials and the presence of the object.
records.limits: Historical Minimalism in art and minimal design in marketing language are different concepts.
records.visual_principles: Form, material, repetition, organization and spatial relationships.

records.contemporary_application: Juxtapose two visual languages on a magazine cover for a deliberate editorial idea; explain why one dominates.
records.exercise: Interpret one headline through two stylistic conflicts and explain how the conflict contributes to its meaning.
records.filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

records.limits: Do not conclude that anything can be mixed freely; legibility and context remain design decisions.
records.visual_principles: Layered references, debate through historical quotation, irony and controlled visual contrast.

records.contemporary_application: Create an energetic event identity with original shapes; keep essential information such as date and place in a calm hierarchy.
records.exercise: Compare an object’s functional diagram with an expressive poster interpretation.
records.filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

records.limits: Memphis is a design group, not a name for all postmodernism or every colorful geometric pattern.
records.visual_principles: Playful scale, unexpected color/form relationships, ornament and debate with modernist expectations.

records.contemporary_application: Develop original rhythmic lettering and forms for a music event; keep essential event information independently readable.
records.exercise: Make one dense and one calm poster; compare how viewers find the message.
records.filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

records.limits: Sensory overload and communication goals differ. Avoid flash/strobe in motion and do not trace existing works.
records.visual_principles: Dense patterns, wandering lines, competing colors and text treated as imagery.

records.contemporary_application: Separate outlines and color layers in an original cover; interpret the formation of print layers in motion as a contemporary proposal.
records.exercise: Add a third layer to a two-color composition; compare alignment with deliberate displacement.
records.filter_note: Asset/medium labels describe our suggested applications, not the historical movement.

records.limits: Do not generalize this as Japanese minimalist style or equate digital layers with historical craft.
records.visual_principles: Registered color blocks, relationships between outlines and layers, and serial production.

records.contemporary_application: Use an original geometric system as a grid or border without reducing an entire culture to one symbol.

records.visual_principles: Repetition, interlacing and expandable arrangements built from circles, squares, stars and polygons.

records.contemporary_application: Determine a community project message with the people involved and create an original rhythm of words and colors.
records.exercise: Create three visual hierarchies for a short community message you wrote.

records.visual_principles: Plural narratives through everyday life, portraiture and different visual media.

exercises.teaching: Weight is a relationship, not an object property. Move the vessel away from the group, then change its scale. Compare the remaining gaps before deciding whether attention moved. Retain three layouts using the same four objects.

The central patch has RGB 128, 128, 128 in every specimen. Predict its appearance before comparing the surrounds. Report a difference or no difference; either is valid evidence. Change one surround, not the patch. Browser display and ambient light are not calibrated print proof.

This original color-plane reconstruction uses unequal rectangular areas and orthogonal boundaries. The retained object positions connect it to our still life, not to a named historical painting. Read S28 before making a historical claim.

studio.limits: Color-plane study only. De Stijl publication, architecture and social aims are not modeled. Historical claims retain S28 review limits.
studio.ownership: Project-authored original; simplified editable reconstruction, not a historical artwork.

regions.explanation: The warm vertical mass sits left of the cooler arch. Its width competes with the surrounding blank space; moving it changes that gap, not just its location.
regions.label: 1 / Vessel weight

regions.explanation: A vertical blue field gives the composition a tall anchor. In the plane study its cutout is simplified to a rectangular interruption, emphasizing orthogonal edges.
regions.label: 2 / Arch boundary

regions.explanation: The pale rounded form becomes a small light rectangle in the plane study. The area stays subordinate to the large blue field; shape and hierarchy are separate decisions.
regions.label: 3 / Light plane

regions.explanation: A low dark form balances the tall left mass. The rectangular reinterpretation removes the diagonal fold rather than pretending to preserve its material.
regions.label: 4 / Dark counterweight

regions.explanation: The open interval below the arch separates the foreground group. Compare the two gaps rather than assuming equal spacing is always balanced.
regions.label: 5 / Unequal intervals
